hook.line: Some things bore you, tire you or get you going, and you want to say so without blaming yourself. In Spanish the thing does it to you. Hernando has a lot to say about meetings with the developer.

examples.es: Me aburre oír siempre lo mismo.
examples.en: It bores me to hear the same thing all the time.

examples.es: Le motiva mucho el proyecto nuevo.
examples.en: The new project really motivates her.
Driving at night tires me out.

examples.es: A Hernando le aburren las reuniones.

examples.en: Waiting so long tires us out.
Does the film bore you? (to a friend)

rule:
Verbs like *aburrir*, *cansar* and *motivar* work like *gustar*. The thing that bores or tires you is the subject, and you are the one who receives it.

*Me aburre la reunión*: the meeting bores me.
*Me aburren las reuniones*: the verb is plural when the thing is.
*Le motiva el proyecto*: the project motivates her.
*Me cansa manejar*: an infinitive counts as one thing.

Add *A Hernando* before *le* to name who. Say *yo aburro*, and you are the boring one.
smallPrint: Teachers call these verbs like *gustar*: the cause is the grammatical subject and the person is an indirect object.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (Meetings bore me): ___ las reuniones. (Me aburre / Me aburren)
yourTurn.why: More than one meeting, so the verb is plural: *aburren*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Driving at night tires me out.
yourTurn.why: The thing is driving, so *cansa*, and *me* is you.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: The new project really motivates her.
yourTurn.answer: Le motiva mucho el proyecto nuevo.
accept: El proyecto nuevo le motiva mucho.
yourTurn.why: *Le* is her, and the project is the thing doing it.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about Hernando: Me cansa manejar de noche.
yourTurn.answer: A Hernando le cansa manejar de noche.
yourTurn.why: Name him with *a Hernando* and switch *me* to *le*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: Me aburre la reunión.
Make it about us: Me aburre esa serie.
yourTurn.why: *Nos* is us, and the verb stays as it is.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend if the film bores them.
yourTurn.why: *Te* is your friend, and the film is the thing.

pitfalls.why: Almost. With *yo aburro* you are the one boring the meetings; let the meetings do it to you.
The meetings do the boring, so the verb is plural.

pitfalls.wrong: Me cansa de manejar de noche.
pitfalls.why: The infinitive follows directly, with no *de*.

personal: Tell us one thing that bores you and one that motivates you. Use *me aburre* and *me motiva*.
